title: Prefetch feedback-loop regression retrospective
author: Elena García
content:
Summary
-------
This retrospective analyzes a production regression that began 2025-11-18 and lasted eight days before automated rollback and operator intervention fully restored expected behavior. The regression manifested as elevated tail-latency and increased miss-rate for LLM KV prefix cache reads for small seqlen workloads, primarily impacting real-time chat endpoints (route: /v1/chat/stream).

Goals of this doc:
- Capture timeline and impact metrics.
- Explain root-cause with causal evidence.
- Document detection rules and mitigations applied.
- Propose preventative changes, tests, and owner assignments.

Timeline (high level)
--------------------
1) 2025-11-18 03:12 UTC — First automated alert: token-latency SLI for /v1/chat/stream breached 99th percentile > 1.5s (SLO target: 99p < 1.0s).
2) 2025-11-18 03:20 UTC — Operators observed rising KV cache miss-rate from 4% baseline to 28% (service: kv-prefetcher).
3) 2025-11-18 04:05 UTC — Canary rollout for a new prefetch heuristic (feature flag: prefetch_v2) had reached 15% overall traffic.
4) 2025-11-19 — Attempts to tune allocator and increase prefetch concurrency caused brief improvements but also produced eviction storms.
5) 2025-11-21 14:32 UTC — Automated rollback to prefetch_v1 completed.
6) 2025-11-22 — Post-rollback monitoring showed residual eviction jitter; final fixes to cache watermarks and operator throttles completed.

Impact summary
--------------
- Affected cohort: 9% of production tenants (mainly PLG chat flows with median request length 64 tokens).
- User-visible latency: 99p token latency increased from 0.9s to 1.8s for affected tenants.
- Cost: approx +12% GPU token compute due to additional model re-generation from cache misses (est. $18k incremental for incident window).
- Pages/ops: 6 on-call shifts across three teams (platform, serving-runtime, eng-sre).

Key observability signals (queries) used during investigation
-----------------------------------------------------------
- KV cache miss-rate (per model, per region):
  sum(rate(kv_cache_misses_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total[5m]))
- Operator eviction events (5m window):
  increase(kv_evictions_total[5m]) > 0
- 99th token latency for streaming route:
  histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/chat/stream"}[5m])) by (le))
- Prefetch queue length by pod:
  max(prefetch_queue_length) by (pod)

Root-cause analysis
-------------------
We performed a phased analysis combining telemetry, canary diffs, and code review. The chain of causation we validated:

1) Behavioral change in prefetch_v2: the new heuristic increased speculative prefetch breadth for short-context requests to attempt better cache-hit coverage. This raised concurrent prefetch tasks per request from median 2 -> 6.
2) KV cache watermark math bug: a 32-bit integer truncation in the new watermarks computation caused watermarks to appear higher than actual available capacity, delaying evictions until memory pressure was critical.
3) Eviction storms: when memory pressure finally triggered, the delayed eviction path forced many large shard-level evictions. That caused temporary read failures and serialization stalls in the prefix cache read path, increasing miss-rate and tail-latency.
4) Feedback amplification: the higher miss-rate led clients to re-request prefixes and fall back to slower full token generation paths, increasing load and causing more prefetch tasks and further pressure (positive feedback loop).

Evidence checklist (what we observed)
- Canary vs baseline: canary prefetch_v2 at 15% had miss-rate 3x baseline and 99p latency +0.9s.
- Heap/memory traces: pods with prefetch_v2 reported delayed GC and higher RSS peaks prior to eviction logs.
- Code diff: watermarks function used int32 arithmetic in an allocator loop where expected values exceeded 2^31-1 for certain shard aggregates.
- Repro: Local replay harness reproduces miss-rate increase when prefetch concurrency simulated at real traffic levels (see appendix for replay command).

Mitigations applied during incident (chronological)
------------------------------------------------
1) 2025-11-18 05:00 UTC — Scoped rollback: reduced canary traffic to 2% and disabled speculative prefetch breadth expansion (feature flag set to conservative).
2) 2025-11-18 07:45 UTC — Emergency operator step: manually lowered shard watermarks to force earlier evictions (operator runbook: prefetch-eviction-manual).
3) 2025-11-19 10:20 UTC — Autoscaler throttle added to prefetch queue to cap per-pod prefetch worker count at 8.
4) 2025-11-21 14:32 UTC — Full rollback: prefetch_v1 promoted and prefetch_v2 rolled back fleet-wide.

Permanent corrective actions and timeline
---------------------------------------
We agreed the following backlog items and owners. Priority assignments indicated: P0 (week), P1 (30 days), P2 (quarter).

- P0: Fix allocator integer truncation and add unit tests (owner: eng-serving-runtime — Priya Nair)
- P0: Add canary test that simulates high concurrency small-seqlen traffic in replay harness (owner: eng-platform QA — Marcus Lee)
- P0: Short-term: change default prefetch breadth for short seqlen to previous heuristic (owner: product/platform — Elena García)
- P1: Introduce an eviction early-warning metric (eviction_pressure_score) and dashboard tile (owner: eng-sre)
- P1: Add operator CTA to abort canary if kv_cache_miss_rate > 10% within 30 minutes (owner: oncall tooling)
- P2: Capacity-simulation job that verifies prefetch + cache interactions at scale as part of CI gate (owner: eng-infra)

Action-items table
------------------
| id | action | owner | priority | due |
|----|--------|-------|----------|-----|
| A1 | Fix 32-bit truncation and add unit/regression tests | Priya Nair | P0 | 2025-11-19 |
| A2 | Replay test for canary profile + automation pass/fail | Marcus Lee | P0 | 2025-11-26 |
| A3 | Dashboard: eviction_pressure_score and alert | Daniel Ho (eng-sre) | P1 | 2025-12-10 |
| A4 | Prefetch feature flag safety gate in rollout system | Elena García | P0 | 2025-11-25 |
| A5 | Runbook: automatic canary abort on miss-rate > X | Eng-Platform / Oncall Tools | P1 | 2025-12-05 |

Detection and alerting improvements (playbook changes)
-----------------------------------------------------
- New derived SLI: "kv_eviction_pressure_score"
  - Definition: weighted combination of increase(kv_evictions_total[5m]), rss_growth_rate, and prefetch_queue_length.
  - Alert threshold (SEV-2 candidate): kv_eviction_pressure_score > 0.65 for 10 minutes.
- Canary rollout safety gate: fail canary if canary_kv_miss_rate / baseline_kv_miss_rate > 2.0 for 15 minutes.
- Dashboard tiles to add: per-model miss-rate heatmap, eviction_pressure_score trend, canary vs baseline latency diff.

Operator runbook excerpt: immediate steps for suspected prefetch regression
---------------------------------------------------------------------
1) Identify whether a canary rollout is in progress: kubectl get rollout feature/prefetch_v2 --namespace=platform
2) If canary > 5% traffic, immediately reduce to 1% and pause rollout.
3) Query miss-rate: run monitoring query above; if miss-rate > 10% for 15m, escalate to eng-serving-runtime owner.
4) Apply emergency watermark correction (only if evictions > 0 and memory RSS > 80%): run internal script /opt/platform/bin/eviction_force.sh --shard <id> --delta -0.15
5) If manual changes not effective within 30m, rollback the feature flag to previous version.

Post-incident verification criteria
---------------------------------
The incident is considered contained when all of these are true for 48 hours:
- kv_cache_miss_rate <= 5% for all models and regions.
- 99p token latency for /v1/chat/stream within SLO (<=1.0s).
- Eviction events reduced to baseline (no sustained >2x baseline for 24h).

Longer-term roadmap items (informed by this retrospective)
--------------------------------------------------------
- Platform roadmap Q1 2026: prioritize CI-grade workload replay and operator-in-the-loop canary automation.
- Q2 2026: integrate prefetch simulation into capacity forecasting engine to estimate unit-cost impact of heuristic changes.

Lessons learned and principles reinforced
---------------------------------------
- Canary safety gates must include cross-system metrics (prefetch behavior + downstream cache health), not just route latency.
- Small arithmetic/overflow bugs in allocation math can produce outsized production effects; integer-size assumptions must be codified in design docs and tested.
- Operators need concise, executable CTAs (scripts + runbook steps) for rapid remediation; we added cheatsheets to the operator-runbook repo.

Appendix
--------
Reproduction command (replay harness):
```
# replay traffic using canary profile (token lengths ~ 40-80)
./replay-harness --profile canary_small_seqlen --inject-prefetch-concurrency 6 --duration 30m --report=./reports/canary-run.json
```
Relevant diffs (high level):
- prefetch/heuristics.go: speculativeBreadth changed from func(old) -> new function scaling by request.sigConfidence; introduced new concurrency path.
- allocator/watermarks.go: used int32 for aggregateShardCount; fixed to int64 and added overflow checks.
